Dana — thanks for the clear list. Summary below; attaching our retention matrix (retention-matrix-v2.xlsx) and an internal playbook excerpt (erasure-evidence-playbook.pdf). High-level answers first, then specifics.

High level (hosted API defaults, US region):
- Raw requests (prompts): default capture window is 30 days; after that data is removed from primary hot stores and subject to tombstone/short-term archive for an additional 30 days solely for debug/rollback; fully purged at 60 days by default unless account-level retention overrides apply.
- Streamed token fragments: not persisted by default in long-term stores. Streaming buffers are ephemeral (kept in memory and short-lived caches) and flushed within 24 hours; only finalized completions are written to persistent stores.
- KV cache / session state: session-level KV caches used to accelerate inference are ephemeral and live for the life of the session; default TTL is 24 hours. For interactive sessions flagged as "persistent" by customers, TTL is configurable.
- Final outputs / completions: default retention is 90 days for hosted accounts (used for billing, troubleshooting, and quality monitoring). Customers can opt-in to longer retention or an auto-delete policy via account settings or API flags.

Residency (US region): default persisted artifacts are stored in US-specific cloud regions (us-west-2 and us-east-1 replicas depending on routing). Ephemeral caches may only exist in the serving zone (no cross-region replication unless the customer requests multi-region).

Proof of deletion / evidence:
- We provide an exportable erasure record for customer-initiated deletions showing the artifact id, timestamp (ISO8601), deletion method (api/console/auto-ttl), and cryptographic hash of the object prior to deletion when applicable.
- For default TTL purges (e.g., the 60-day purge for prompts), we can supply batch deletion manifests on request (CSV/JSON) and an internal audit log extract showing deletion jobs and timestamps.
- For Dedicated & Private: Dedicated uses customer-dedicated pools; defaults are configurable at contract time (we recommend contractually specifying retention). Private (VPC/on-prem) means Redwood does not persist to Redwood-managed storage by default; the customer controls storage and erasure.

Next steps:

- Kim (legal/privacy) has offered a short contract-friendly paragraph we can include in an addendum — cc'd.
- If helpful we can produce a one-off deletion certificate for backlog data; need a signed request form and a window (we usually respond within 5 business days).

Happy to jump on a 30-min sync if you want to walk the matrix live.

Dana / Karthik — brief legal/controls wording below you can reference in your InfoSec questionnaire. I'm keeping this high-level; for contract language we can provide a short DPA addendum.

Authoritative statement for default hosted accounts (US):
- Redwood Inference maintains the following default retention policy for hosted platform accounts unless explicitly changed by customer configuration or contract: prompts (30 days, plus a 30-day tombstone window), ephemeral streaming buffers (no default persistent storage; flushed within 24 hours), KV/session caches (default TTL 24 hours), final completions (90 days).
- Residency: persisted artifacts for US-region accounts reside within Redwood-managed resources in US cloud regions (primary: us-west-2; secondary replication for high-availability may include us-east-1).
- Deletion evidence: Redwood maintains immutable audit logs for deletion jobs and can provide customer-facing deletion manifests which include object identifiers, pre-deletion hashes, S3/cluster paths (redacted as needed), timestamps, and the operator/service that executed the job. For regulated customers requiring chain-of-custody or notarized certificates, Redwood can support an enhanced evidence package as a professional services engagement.

Dedicated & Private:
- Dedicated: retention defaults may be set at the account level during onboarding and documented in the order form.
- Private: control plane connectivity and storage behavior depend on deployment model; Redwood's default persistence does not apply to customer-managed on-prem environments.

Let me know if you need this framed as a single-paragraph statement for the procurement workbook; I can draft it.
